clue.text: Completed attempt to undertake risky contract

parts.note: something completed is over, finished
a bid is an attempt, as in a bid for freedom

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their effort to take on a dangerous deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the bid sets the contract a side must make; bidding beyond what the hand can deliver is taking on a risky contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid too high, especially at cards, commits you to a contract you may well fail to make.

clue.text: Curse part of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a region of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath like 'Oh, blast!' is a curse, and an oblast is an administrative region of Russia.

clue.text: Distributing medicine, one eliminated disease in region

indicators.note: distributing means spreading out, so the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
eliminated means the one is taken out of the word medicine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Handing out drugs wiped out a local illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminated' removes I (one) from MEDICINE, leaving MEDCINE, which 'Distributing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic, as a noun, is an illness regularly found among people of a particular area.

clue.text: Porter's sources include reference book that's to the point

parts.note: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable is a well-known reference book
i.e., id est, means that is
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A railway porter's sources include a handbook that is concise.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is a dark beer, not a luggage carrier. BREWER'S is a classic British reference dictionary of phrase and fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, and it comes from the places where beer is made.

clue.text: Call the tune? Promises to pay

explanation.surface: Dictating the music, and also a set of IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisting on musical sounds is calling the tune; promissory paper payable on request is a financial instrument.

clue.text: Management problem for a few

explanation.surface: A small crew turns out to be a headache for the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hard to control is called a real handful, and a handful is also a small number, as many as a hand holds.

clue.text: Name associated with male or female

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A question of whether a name goes with a man or a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female bird, and loosely any female.

clue.text: Relative, in time, acted every other character

indicators.note: every other character means taking alternate letters, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A family member who, in due course, played every second role.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Game to include jazz piece in medley

indicators.note: to include means the game takes the jazz piece inside it

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game
a rag is a piece of ragtime

explanation.surface: A game featuring a jazz number in a musical mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble or hotchpotch of things.

clue.text: Displayed by Scrooge at first, say? No, only at the end

definitions.text: Displayed by Scrooge at first, say? No, only at the end

parts.words: Displayed by Scrooge at first, say? No, only at the end
parts.note: Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is mean at first and only becomes openhanded after the ghosts visit

explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving, which the miser shows only after his Christmas reform.

clue.text: This type is male and promiscuous?

definitions.text: This type is male and promiscuous?

indicators.note: promiscuous means indiscriminate and mixed up, so the three words before it are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what sort of man sleeps around.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'promiscuous' scrambles IS MALE AND, and the result is the kind of man who chases women.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is a man who pursues many women, the very type the clue describes.

clue.text: Note nothing in basic education that's a mistake

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: in places the nought within the three Rs

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of schooling
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint that a gap in schooling fundamentals is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Approximately 1, 000 in battle

indicators.note: in puts the thousand inside the word for about

parts.note: some means about, as in some twenty people
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An estimate of a thousand soldiers taking part in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme was the 1916 First World War battle in northern France, named after its river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme names a famous First World War engagement of 1916.

clue.text: Parisian sight not concerning American woman

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, regarding
dame is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A tourist landmark in Paris, said to have nothing to do with an American lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité is one of the city's chief tourist attractions.

clue.text: Noble champion

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who is also the reigning winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer bears a rank such as earl, and a reigning sports winner holds the championship.

clue.text: Warning of engagement?

parts.note: engagement looks like a betrothal, but here it is a battle, and the warning is the call for crews to man their posts

explanation.definitionFit: The order on a warship to go to battle positions alerts everyone that combat is imminent.

clue.text: Cheats watch clock

explanation.surface: Swindlers keep an eye on the time.
explanation.walkthrough: A watch and a clock are a pair of timepieces, read playfully as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithful lovers are deceivers, and a wristwatch plus a wall clock make a pair of timepieces.

clue.text: Protective cover quickly added to vehicle

indicators.note: added to means the speedy word is tacked on after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means swiftly

explanation.surface: A protective covering is speedily fitted to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shell on the back of a tortoise or crab shields its body.

clue.text: General way in which men progress

explanation.surface: A remark on how soldiers advance under a commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to everyone alike means universal, and chess or draughts pieces (called men) move over the playing surface.

clue.text: Stand once more? On the contrary

definitions.text: Stand once more? On the contrary

parts.words: Stand once more? On the contrary
parts.note: to stand someone a drink again is to treat them anew, while the opposite of standing your ground is falling back

explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal or falling back is the opposite of holding firm.

clue.text: Fairly consistently with the truth

explanation.surface: Justly and accurately done.
explanation.definitionFit: Justly or with good reason, and also correctly or accurately.

clue.text: Sentimental traveller in Western Europe

indicators.note: in tells us the name lies inside the words Western Europe

explanation.surface: An emotional tourist on the western side of the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote A Sentimental Journey through France and Italy, so he is the sentimental traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of A Sentimental Journey, the eighteenth-century novelist who toured France and Italy.

clue.text: Course in opposition to priest, mainly

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pastor is a minister or priest

explanation.surface: Someone takes a course of study set up against the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests study, but it is a stage of a meal: the Italian starter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats and pickles served as the first dish of a meal.

clue.text: Cushion against gold going up in the City

parts.note: a pad is a cushion

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A cushion props up gold rising in value in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests London's financial district, but it is just a city, in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Padua is a university city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Form gold initially into this

indicators.note: form means shape or mould, so the letters are moulded into a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of the word gold

explanation.surface: An instruction to cast gold into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: G (the first letter of 'gold') with INTO, rearranged as 'Form' says, makes the bar that gold is cast into.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten precious metal is cast into a bar or block for storage.

clue.text: One point in the lead

parts.note: a means one
a head is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A single point decides who is leading.
explanation.definitionFit: In front of the others, leading the field.

clue.text: Dog for Russian composer

parts.note: Red is old shorthand for a Soviet Russian
a setter composes, whether type or a crossword

explanation.surface: A dog named after a Russian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian composer' suggests Tchaikovsky and friends, but the composer is a setter, and the Russian is a Red.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter, a gundog breed with a glossy chestnut coat.

clue.text: Abandon competitor in tough race

explanation.surface: Quitting a gruelling contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon, and a participant in the rat race is the hard-driven careerist.

clue.text: Competitor in point-to point galloped in race

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
N, north, is another compass point

indicators.note: in places the running inside the motorcycle race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
galloped means ran

explanation.surface: A rider in a steeplechase gallops in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point-to-point' looks like the British amateur steeplechase, but it gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has entered a race or contest is a participant in it.

clue.text: Tersely ordered to change formation

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Briskly told to switch formation, like troops on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new design or form, as a hairdresser reshapes a cut.
